mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected corporate cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns do not fall below the 10th percentile of same-month pre-rate increases during confirmed tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly pay growth acceleration (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% above the prior month's rate coincides with higher consumer confidence and corporate hiring intentions, which elevates expected future earnings and drives positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, SPX 60-day forward returns remain non-significantly different from a baseline of zero when PAYEMS acceleration is present.

mechanism_narrative: When the seasonally adjusted RSAFS (retail sales) unexpectedly exceeds prior month by more than 2%, it indicates resilient consumer demand, which raises expectations for corporate profits and supports a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: During confirmed demand shocks, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically higher than during neutral RSAFS growth periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 3% suggests supply-side constraints, which raises uncertainty and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -3% month-over-month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: During confirmed supply shocks, 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than in a structural supply expansion baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of falling CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 2% for three consecutive months reduces discounting of future cash flows, supporting positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: During sustained low inflation, SPX 20-day returns fail to outperform a 1% risk-free rate benchmark.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment) falls by more than 0.5 percentage points in a month, it signals labor market tightening that raises expected wage growth and corporate profits, pushing S&P 500 20-day forward returns higher.
failure_condition: During unemployment declines, SPX 20-day returns do not exceed the 95th percentile of prior tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both FEDFUNDS and HOUST (home sales) over the same month create a dual headwind: higher rates depress discounting while weak housing demand lowers growth expectations, jointly depressing S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
regime_hint: Dual contractionary monetary and housing cycle
failure_condition: During simultaneous declines in both proxies, SPX 20-day returns do not fall as predicted compared to baseline scenarios.

mechanism_narrative: During a post-COVID recovery regime (as indicated by high GDPC1 growth and low UNRATE), S&P 500 60-day forward returns tend to be positive due to optimism about economic reopening and corporate earnings recovery.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 5% and UNRATE < 4% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: In the defined regime, 60-day forward returns are not consistently positive across multiple market stress tests.
